summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive web app that uses NASA lunar data to help users explore potential landing sites. Users select a research area on a 3D globe or 2D map, set a search radius and mission dates, and compare nearby sites based on sunlight, estimated solar energy, Earth visibility, terrain, and temperature. The app also shows where permanent shadow may make an area worth investigating for water ice.

With What IF, users can see how a mission delay, a change in landing location, or both could affect their options. Professional mode shows the evidence and limits behind each assessment, while Education mode helps learners explore the trade-offs of landing on the Moon. By making lunar data easier to use, the app helps users identify promising sites for further study and understand how timing and location shape a mission.
details:
LUNAR — Lunar Landing Site Navigator


Choosing a lunar landing site means looking beyond coordinates. A location may offer sunlight but limited Earth visibility, while nearby terrain can introduce long shadows and difficult operating conditions. LUNAR brings these factors into one browser-based workspace, helping users explore a practical question: Where and when could a lunar mission operate, and what challenges would it face?
Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, our project helps mission planners, researchers, educators and the public compare candidate locations and mission windows. Users can examine sunlight availability, Earth-centre visibility, terrain characteristics and historical temperature evidence through visual timelines, comparative assessments and explained research scores.


LUNAR connects site assessment with mission planning. Using NASA/JPL Horizons positions, LOLA terrain data and Diviner temperature observations, it brings together evidence that would otherwise require separate analysis. Its Mission Planner lets users enter solar-panel specifications, battery capacity and operating loads to estimate generation, battery charge and periods of insufficient electrical supply. Users can also test a change to their configuration, save searches and export reports documenting their results and assumptions.


By bringing these tools together, LUNAR gives astronauts and engineers a shared platform to explore mission challenges, compare options and work from the same information. We also introduce Education Mode, helping the public, educators and students explore lunar conditions and understand mission-planning concepts through accessible explanations and visualisations.


Our aim is to make lunar exploration easier to understand while keeping the evidence transparent. LUNAR presents data sources, missing information and model limitations alongside its findings. It supports early exploration and learning, with research assessments and simplified simulations that require further engineering verification before real mission use.

What It Does and How It Works

·  Select your mission details to start searching for suitable landing point. Select past mission site, landmarks or select your own custom location

· Get research area research value potential by selecting research focus (Mapped permanant shadow percentage will be given if the research focus is water-ice at Lunar south pole)

2. Compare page

· Compare up to 2 alternatives with multiple criteria rating
